Repository re-linked. Your files now appear as changes compared with GitHub.

branch %1$s will be created on GitHub

GitHub commits will be merged into your branch
The workflow file is invalid or no job could start.
Open .github/workflows/*.yml and check indentation and \"on: workflow_dispatch\", or recreate the file from the app (Diagnose project).
The file google-services.json is missing, so the Firebase plugin cannot run.
Add google-services.json inside the app folder (download it from Firebase Console) and publish again.
google-services.json does not contain this app package name.
In Firebase Console add an Android app with the same package name as applicationId, download the new google-services.json and replace the old one.
Kotlin code uses a name that does not exist (a missing import, a typo or a missing library).
Open the file and line shown in the evidence, fix the name or add the import or dependency, then publish again.
Fix the first error in the evidence (file:line). Later errors are often caused by it.
Fix the first error in the evidence (file:line), then publish again.
An Android resource (string, color, drawable or style) is missing or invalid.
Find the resource named in the evidence and add it under app/src/main/res, or fix the reference to it.
AndroidManifest.xml conflicts with a library manifest.
Read the manifest line in the evidence, then fix the duplicated or missing attribute (or use tools:replace).
Two copies of the same class or resource were found.
Remove the duplicated library or file, or exclude one copy in the Gradle dependencies.
A Gradle plugin was not found or has no version.
Declare the plugin with a version in the root build.gradle.kts and check the repositories in settings.gradle.kts.
Gradle could not download a library (wrong name or version, or the repository is unavailable).
Check the dependency name and version in app/build.gradle.kts and make sure google() and mavenCentral() are listed.
Gradle cannot find the module or task that the workflow builds (:app:assembleDebug).
Make sure settings.gradle.kts includes \":app\" and that the workflow command matches your module name.
Signing failed: the keystore file or its password is wrong or missing.
Make sure app/liblink.keystore is pushed to GitHub and the passwords in app/build.gradle.kts match it.
The build ran out of memory.
Add org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx3g to gradle.properties or reduce the size of the project.
The Java version of the build does not match the project.
Use Java 17 in the workflow (setup-java) and set Java 17 compatibility in app/build.gradle.kts.
An Android SDK component required by the project is missing on the build server.
Lower compileSdk or targetSdk to a version available on GitHub, or install the missing platform in the workflow.
The Gradle wrapper is missing or not executable.
The default workflow runs gradle without a wrapper. If you use gradlew, upload the gradle/wrapper folder and make gradlew executable.
The build finished but the APK was not found where the workflow expects it.
Make sure the workflow uploads app/build/outputs/apk/debug/*.apk and that your module is named app.
GitHub refused the action because the workflow has no permission.
In the repository Settings → Actions → General allow read and write permissions, or add a permissions block to the workflow.
A GitHub Action used by the workflow does not exist or its version is wrong.
Check the \"uses:\" lines in the workflow and use valid versions such as actions/checkout@v4.
The code could not be fetched from the repository.
Check that the repository exists, the branch name is right and the repository access is allowed.
Preparing the build environment (Java or Gradle) failed.
Check the setup-java and setup-gradle steps and their versions in the workflow, then run again.
The app build failed, but the log has no known error pattern.
Open the evidence lines below and the full log in GitHub (Open in GitHub) to find the first error.
Check the upload step path in the workflow and that the build produced an APK.
Check the repository workflow permissions and the release step in the workflow.
The build failed in an unknown step.
Open the full log in GitHub (Open in GitHub) and look for the first red error.
No builds recorded yet. Run a build first.
First release with a known size
Size not loaded yet. Tap Refresh.

Email/Password sign-in is not enabled in Firebase Authentication.
Cloud sync is not configured in this build.

Restore the library and settings as they were before the last sync that changed them?

The folders are kept inside the ZIP. Import it with \"Import ZIP update\" to restore everything with its folders, or share it.
